messages:
oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-0432 created — elevated 5xx rate observed in runtime (us-west-2). Paging @eng-oncall @runtime-oncall @infra-oncall. Auto-detection flagged runtime-32 shard.

maria: I'm on this as primary for now. Spike started ~10:12 UTC, affecting hosted API customers in us-west-2 (token generations failing with 503/504).

devon: Switching to primary in 2m to take mitigation. I'll grab logs + routing table. Runbook ref: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/runtime-5xx (sec 2).

rachel: Support note: ticket #12345 from PineNotes reporting repeated timeouts. I can confirm 4 orgs showing >50% error rate. Posting customer impact to status page now.

sam: Quick infra check — nodes in that AZ show GPU driver restarts and memory pressure on r-node-17. Could be underlying node instability.

maria: Handing to @devon (primary) / @maria (secondary). Also flagging a coverage gap tonight 22:00-02:00 UTC — ana is OOO; if this escalates late, we may need to pull in off-shift infra.

devon: Starting mitigation: cordon + drain r-node-17 and restart runtime-32 pod set. Commands I'm running:
```
kubectl cordon r-node-17
kubectl drain r-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
kubectl rollout restart deploy/runtime-32 -n runtime-prod\```

devon: tailing logs after restart: `kubectl logs -n runtime-prod deploy/runtime-32 --tail=200` — watching for repeated stack traces / OOM messages.

sam: infra logs show OOM kill around 10:08 and kernel messages referencing nvidia driver crash. I'm checking instance metrics and autoscaler decisions. If driver crash, infra-oncall takes lead for node remediation.

security-oncall: I don't see unusual auth or exfiltration patterns in the initial window. No indicators of compromise so far; will continue monitoring traffic signatures.

rachel: I'll prepare templated customer update: "Customers in US-WEST may see intermittent 5xx errors for up to 15 minutes while we remediate. Engineers are investigating." Posting to status.redwood now :warning:
notes:
maria: If 5xx persists after restart, fallback routing to smaller model-variant is allowed per routing playbook. Command to trigger fallback (ops console):

`curl -X POST https://console.redwood/api/v1/ops/fallback -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"service":"runtime","force":true}'`

maria: Cross-team routing pointers: runtime owns application-layer failures (model runtime, KV cache, request handling). Infra owns node/driver/kernel/instance issues. Security gets looped for anomalous traffic or credential misuse. Support owns customer comms + ticket triage.

devon: After restart error rate dropped from ~18% -> ~2% in 6m. Staying on for 30m monitoring then will hand back to maria.

oncall-bot: Handoff recorded: primary=devon -> maria at 2762345978.

maria: Thanks — I'll take it back. Will update rotation docs and note the coverage gap for tonight. Will follow up with a short postmortem if we see recurrence. :thumbsup:
